wrong: run the gate first and fix whatever it names
right: dictionary order, then splits, then glyphs, then grammar, then the gate
why: ORDER and SPLITS are about the master, and a gate that fails on them tells you nothing about the spec. Running it early wastes the round trip.

does: text -> marks. Emits RULES, the resolved DATA block, CODE, and a COMPILE REPORT.
guarantees: a word becomes a mark only if the base has that mark; quotes and {} are never rewritten
does_not: it does not check that the spec is correct - it compiles a wrong spec faithfully
tells_you: tokens with no glyph left as text
words the base does not define
trap: the report deduplicates, so one message can stand for ten places. grep, do not trust the count

does: compiles () and [] contents; {} stays a free-form custom block
guarantees: a word inside a paren is a word and becomes a mark, unless it is quoted or the spec declared it
does_not: it cannot tell a pin name from a parameter name - both are just words in the spec
why: a command written as check(x) used to sit inside the paren and never compile at all

does: the single verdict. 13 checks over the dictionary, the mark table and every spec in scope.
guarantees: one PASS/FAIL, and the baseline records what is already known debt
does_not: it does not run the IDE. vibide.py --exam is a different thing and misses everything here
order: SPELL is a grammar check over specs, not over DATA/*.txt prose
trap: --fix rewrites files. read the diff before committing it

does: the checks are ORDER, SPLITS, GLYPHS, DICT, HEADER, PROSE, INHERIT, CUT, ENGLISH, BINDING, SPELL, SYMBOLS, TWICE
guarantees: TWICE is the one that catches a compiler that is not idempotent
does_not: a green gate does not mean the spec is a good IDE - it means the spec is well formed

does: per-spec grammar: nesting, parents, action verbs, pins, arrows, type words, id binding
guarantees: an id may not take a base word, an id is unique per spec, and id and param share one namespace
does_not: it does not compare the spec against the implementation - window.vibe and vibide.py can both pass and still disagree

does: G1-G8 on compiler/symbols_map.txt against the master
guarantees: G5 says the description in symbols_map is byte-identical to the master, so a word lives in three files and all three must agree
does_not: G6 ordering is a warning, not an error - 56 of them stand

does: the dictionary invariants, and it reads DATA/protos.txt too
guarantees: one word one concept, one mark per concept, no abbreviation, no dangling comma
does_not: it does not validate content inside {} or a quoted payload

guarantees: every lesson names a check and a gate, and 0 violations
does_not: a lesson whose gate is listed as absent is a blind spot - 6 of 50 are

cmd: append a JSON line: id, topic, wrong, right, rule, why, check, gate
does: the findings, so a model does not rediscover them by breaking something
guarantees: the format is machine-checked by lessons.py
does_not: it is not training data. 50 lessons is not a dataset for weights, it is a memory for the loop

wrong: the gate is green, so the language is consistent
